To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

carbon taxes are not effective at promoting investment in wind power capacity, that liberalization of electricity markets may reduce investment in wind power, and that fixed price contracts for wind power may be an effective policy to increase investment in renewable capacity.

the intermittent nature of renewable energy technologies drives the effectiveness (or ineffectiveness) of carbon pricing mechanisms to promote investment in renewables, and that market liberalization can reduce investment in renewables while increasing the overall systems cost and emissions.

the intermittency inherent in renewable technologies drives the cost effectiveness of carbon pricing policies, that liberalization may reduce the investment in renewable capacity, and that fixed price contracts with renewable suppliers may be an alternative way to encourage investment in renewable generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the strategic investment decisions of a vertically integrated utility in the context of a competitive market with intermittent supply of renewable electricity.
the effect of carbon pricing on the cost and quantity of wind power in an electricity system.
how the intermittency of electricity generated by renewable technologies (e.g. solar, wind, geothermal) affects the incentives for investing in such technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The intermittency of renewable technology drives the effectiveness of the carbon pricing mechanisms, and thus charging more for emissions can unexpectedly discourage investment in renewable capacity.
the intermittency effect of wind generation is a key determinant of the effectiveness of carbon taxes in promoting investment in wind generation.

(1) the intermittency of renewables is a key factor in the effectiveness of policies aimed at promoting investment in these technologies and (2) the effects of carbon pricing mechanisms are not always as expected, especially in the context of partial liberalization of electricity markets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
carbon taxes may be a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for investment in renewable capacity.
the intermittency problem is the most significant barrier to renewable energy investment, and the intermittency problem will be exacerbated by carbon pricing.
the intermittency in renewable energy supply is a major barrier to the adoption of renewables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intermittency problem of renewable technologies can undermine the effectiveness of carbon taxes as a mechanism for promoting investment in renewables.
the intermittency problem may be the most important obstacle to renewable electricity development.

the intermittency problem is a key factor in the economics of renewable energy, and the design of policies aimed at increasing renewable capacity must take into account this feature of renewable technology.
